title: Community rewind: Carmen Lazar
alt: Carmen Lazar in an Assyrian Podcast rewind post
caption:
Our newest rewind recommendation takes us back to Fairfield, NSW, Australia, in the hub of Assyrian-Australian resettlement community, where we get reacquainted with the ever-lovely Carmen Lazar (@carmenlazar_) 🇦🇺

Carmen Lazar was born in Tehran, Iran and migrated to Australia in 1971. After teaching at the Assyrian School in Sydney and serving in the Assyrian Australian Association, Carmen then became the lead for the Assyrian Resource Centre (ARC) 👩‍🏫, established by the Assyrian Australian Association to serve and empower Assyrians recently arrived in Australia. Carmen has worked at the ARC for over 20 years, helping thousands of Assyrian families settle in Australia and was awarded the Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) in 2014 for her service to her cultural and local communities 🎖

🗣 In this interview, she discusses the many rewarding moments in her work, as well as challenging topics such as domestic abuse and how she’s created opportunities for more people to feel comfortable to speak up.

Since her episode in 2022, she continues her work integrating Assyrian immigrants safely into Australia through the ARC and can be found at most local community events and workshops endorsing all things beneficial to the local community 🌏. Politically, she served as a Fairfield City Council member for Labor, before stepping down and criticising the party’s failure to support initiatives promised to build the community, such as equipment upgrades to local hospitals. She continues her work building relationships within the local community and is currently advocating for 2026 Census Field Officers to go door-to-door to help newly arrived members of the community complete the census correctly and ensure Assyrians are accurately identified 📝 What a woman!

Find out more about her initiatives on her page @carmenlazar_

#AssyrianPodcast
note: A community-service story from Fairfield, New South Wales.

title: Dropping beats with DJ Ano
caption:
🎉 DROPPING BEATS AND TAKING NAMES - IT'S TIME FOR EPISODE 2️⃣1️⃣9️⃣ 🎧

We are so excited to be joined in today's episode with Ano Memari (@dj.ano408), an Assyrian DJ local to the San Francisco Bay Area who plays any and all functions you can think of: weddings, parties, galas, fundraisers, clubs, churches, conventions, festivals - you name it, he's played it. His M.O. for remixing music sets involves incorporating contemporary pop music with Assyrian classics you know and love into a smooth blend of swaying beats and khigga kicks for you to enjoy and dance the night away. Catch a few samples in today's episode scattered throughout to get a taste of DJ Ano's vibes 🕺💃

He also operates Epic Music Entertainment, a local music entertainment company for hosting an array of entertainment services, continuing its work and aspirations after his friend's passing. He's available to book but be quick - he books up months in advance!

In this episode hosted by AP master Mark (@mister_lights), you will hear:
🎼 How his relationship with music developed over the years and allowed him to hone in on what he wants to do to make his mark in the community
🎷 The importance of his Assyrian identity in his music sets and how he uses it to educate listeners on the amazing talent of the Assyrian musician library
🎧 His creative process for creating music, how to set-up staging for an event, and his mindset with the joys and responsibilities of controlling music at a function
🎭 How he uses his best and worst sets to always improve on his craft to satisfaction
🌉 The origins of his company and what he has in store for the future

title: Comedy with Chris Halef
alt: Episode 218 artwork featuring comedian Chris Halef
caption:
EPISODE 2️⃣1️⃣8️⃣ is here and for today's episode, we caught up with Assyrian-Canadian comedian Chris Halef (@chrishalef) whose story about storytelling is one worth hearing 🗣

Growing up in Halifax, Nova Scotia 🇨🇦, life was certainly interesting for Halef when your family is the only Assyrians in town. With his brother by his side, his father unknowingly introduced his sons to the age-inappropriateness of Chris Rock and Dave Chappelle comedy specials, where these had such a profound impact on Halef that he would go around the schoolyard quoting these specials from memory - much to the horror of his teachers! 🏫 Despite being known as the quiet kid, he always kept the passion for laughter and used this courage to overcome his fear of public speaking and build resilience in life as he jumped from journalism into comedy. Ultimately, Halef feels his comedy pursuit has made him bulletproof to embarrassment (for now) 🛡 and is on the rise with an endless supply of anecdotes under his belt thanks to his trademark Assyrian stubbornness.

In this episode, we sit down with Chris to talk about:

🌍 how his family found their way to the East Coast,
🚸 his journey from youth to journalism to stand-up comedy,
🎤 taking on stand-up at age 28 with quirky anecdotes and what his heritage means to him both on and off the stage.

With his videos reminiscing on motifs of growing up in Middle Eastern households, to clips from his taped shows about personal dating vs family stories, Halef's most known for his viral video about speaking the same language as Jesus ✝️ with the video brandishing over 24k likes, and the counter continues to rise!

title: Remembering Narsai David
alt: A tribute to chef and philanthropist Narsai David
caption:
Time for another be kind and rewind back to episode 142 with the incredible Narsai David as he joined the Assyrian Podcast to discuss his upbringing, his career in food and wine, his devotion to his Assyrian heritage, and all the other good things in life 🙏🏼

Narsai David was born in Indiana, U.S. in 1936 where he had a long and successful career in the food and wine industry, from catering to the most famous Rock & Roll bands to opening the renowned Narsai’s Restaurant. He is credited as a published author, radio and T.V. personality, and a humanitarian; raising millions for Assyrian aid through the prestigious “Narsai’s Taste of Mediterranean” event held annually by the Assyrian Aid Society. Despite his personal success, Narsai always made it a point to weave parts of his Assyrian heritage with what he loved through food and wine. 🍷

In the episode, he talked about his incorporation of calligraphy by the late Assyrian calligrapher, Issa Benyamin, on his wine labels and the controversy it received, as well as how one of his most famous and popular dishes at Narsai’s restaurant was his Assyrian leg of lamb 🍽

✝️ He also credited his initial connection to the Assyrian community through church; even being ordained as a deacon of the Assyrian Church of the East and helping to start the Mar Narsai Parish in San Francisco ⛪️

Additionally, he contributed significantly to the Assyrian Aid Society, becoming the Chairman Emeritus and his many contributions include the prestigious “Narsai's Taste of the Mediterranean” annual event, which has raised millions for Assyrian humanitarian aid 🏠👨‍👩‍👧‍👦

Since the episode's original airing in 2021, Narsai sadly passed away on June 20th 2024, a week shy of his 88th birthday. But this loud and proud personality is anything but forgotten by the lives he touched. Chef, radio personality, philanthropist, entrepreneur, former AASA Director and friend to all - Narsai's passion for his Assyrian roots and local community ensures his legacy is, well, legendary 🌏

caption:

No doubt you would have heard her music at some point in your life or come across her name in conversation with the aunties. Now get to hear the first hand experience of growing up with Shamiram's passion and talent for entertaining while maintaining a multicultural home in a new country 🎙🎶✨️

title: Identity, service, and sacrifice
alt: Episode 217 part one artwork featuring Danial Dino Pick
caption:
✨️🎙 EPISODE 217 PART 1 OUT NOW 🎙✨️

In today's episode, we sit down with Retired U.S. Army Colonel Danial "Dino" Pick, whose life bridges the internal conflict of military service in his home country of the U.S., and his Assyrian identity originating in the motherland ⚔️

Over a lustrous 29 year career spanning various special ops missions, he shares the tension of serving as a "foreign power" in his ancestral homeland and his humbling experiences with the local Assyrians 🎖

Colonel Pick opens up about his Assyrian roots growing up in a multi-generational household in the U.S., to joining the U.S. Military and climbing the ranks in language and intelligence specialities with one powerful moment where he reconnects an Assyrian professor with his mother in Alqosh during active combat - you do not want to miss this episode 🎧

This is a story of identity, sacrifice, and honoring a family legacy that continues in Part 2...

#AssyrianPodcast #AssyrianPride #NewEpisode #Assyria

title: Unlocking 6,000 years of history
alt: Episode 215 artwork featuring Assyriologist Dr. Shana S. Zaia
caption:
Meet the Assyrian Assyriologist: Unlocking 6,000 Years of History with Dr. Shana S. Zaia!

What can ancient clay tablets tell us about our modern identity? 📜✨

In our latest episode, we sit down with Dr. Shana S. Zaia, an Assistant Professor at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (@vuamsterdam) and a rare "trifecta" guest: an ASSYRIAN expert studying ancient ASSYRIAN history plus talking to us on the ASSYRIAN Podcast!

Dr. Zaia takes us on a journey through the Neo-Assyrian Empire — the world’s first true global power — and explains how she uses the cuneiform script to "time travel" into the lives of ancient people.

In this episode, we explore:
🫅🏽 The First Empire: How the land of Ashur became a massive territorial state.
✍️ Ancient Homework: What we’ve learned from the discarded tablets of ancient schoolchildren.
🌍 Identity: How being "Assyrian" evolved from a political status to a living cultural heritage.
📚 Outreach: Why preserving the humanities is vital for the future of our community.

Want to dive deeper? Visit shanazaia.com for more resources on learning Akkadian, Sumerian, and our people's epic ancient history.

A huge thank you to our sponsor, Get Set Tech (www.getsettech.com), for supporting our mission to bring Assyrian history to the world! 🙌

title: Reverse migration and The Return
alt: Episode artwork featuring Dilan Adamat of The Return
caption:
In this enlightening episode, we have the privilege of speaking with Dilan Adamat, the founder of The Return—a non-profit organization dedicated to assisting returnees to Mesopotamia, one of the world’s oldest communities. Situated at the crossroads of civilizations between the two rivers, this ancient population stands on the brink of potential extinction, a loss that would be immeasurable for the history and cultural diversity of the Middle East.

Dilan shares the inspiring story behind The Return and its mission to preserve the ancestral heritage of Mesopotamia. We delve into the challenges faced by returnees—whether they’re second- or third-generation young people reconnecting with their roots, families recently displaced, investors, or retirees seeking peace in their homeland. The Return offers personalized support ranging from language courses and professional networking to providing a home base for stays, making the complex journey of returning home a tangible reality.

Join us as we explore the importance of maintaining the rich tapestry of cultures in this historic region and how each of us can play a role in supporting this crucial endeavor. This conversation sheds light on the high stakes involved in preserving Mesopotamia’s ancestral diversity and the collective responsibility we share in safeguarding it for future generations.

Tune in to discover how you can contribute to The Return’s mission and be part of a movement that bridges worlds and unites hearts across distances.
note: A practical conversation about making the journey home possible.
